NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Senior Site Reliability / Platform Engineer
Manchester, UK | nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior platform and reliability engineer with 10 years of experience designing, building and operating infrastructure, including six years running Kubernetes platforms on AWS. Hands-on expertise in Terraform and AWS cloud environments, with a track record of leading technical initiatives from proposal to production. Builds reliable, observable platforms and self-service infrastructure that help product teams deploy and operate services effectively.

CORE SKILLS
Cloud infrastructure: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), cloud environment design and operation
Infrastructure as code: Terraform, Atlantis, Crossplane
Platform and systems: Kubernetes, Helm, Kustomize, Argo CD, Karpenter, Linux
Reliability and observability: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, SLOs and error budgets, incident management
Automation and testing: Go, Python, Bash, GitHub Actions, k6, Puppet

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS)
Manchester / remote | Apr 2022 – Present
- Technical lead for a five-person platform team, operating an AWS EKS platform spanning eight clusters, approximately 350 services and three regions.
- Designed and built an internal developer platform with Go and Python service templates, Argo CD GitOps, and Crossplane-based self-service provisioning for RDS, SQS and S3 through pull requests.
- Enabled adoption of the developer platform across all 14 product teams, reducing the time to take a new service to production from approximately two weeks to under one day.
- Led the SLO programme for the 20 most critical services, introducing burn-rate alerts and an error-budget policy agreed with product leadership; reduced on-call pages by approximately 60%.
- Replaced cluster-autoscaler managed node groups with Karpenter and spot capacity for stateless workloads, including interruption handling; reduced EC2 spend by 38% (approximately GBP 410,000 annually).
- Participate in the incident commander rotation and established the incident and post-mortem process.
- Mentored three engineers transitioning into SRE from backend engineering.

Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games
Leeds | Jan 2019 – Mar 2022
- Operated AWS game backend infrastructure using EC2, ECS and later EKS, supporting titles with up to 1.2 million daily active players.
- Managed AWS infrastructure as code with approximately 40 Terraform modules and used Atlantis for pull-request-based plan and apply workflows.
- Replaced a noisy Nagios setup with a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager and Loki observability stack.
- Ran k6 load tests and led launch capacity planning, including tests simulating 300,000 concurrent players; identified and resolved a connection-pool limit before launch.

Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting
Sheffield | Jul 2016 – Dec 2018
- Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration management.
- Automated operational tasks with Bash and Python and provided on-call support for customer incidents.

SELECTED PROJECT
Kubernetes cleanup controller | Open source side project | 2024
- Built a small Go controller using controller-runtime to delete expired preview namespaces; the project has approximately 120 GitHub stars.

EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016

CERTIFICATIONS
AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional | 2023
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021, renewed 2024

COMMUNITY
Speaker, UK DevOps meetup | 2024
“SLOs that product managers care about”

LANGUAGES
English (native) | Urdu (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, professional, evidence-based CV with clear section headings, substantial technical depth, and excellent quantified outcomes. The experience section shows progression from Linux systems engineering into senior platform and reliability leadership. Metrics such as 350 services, 14 product teams, 60% fewer on-call pages, 38% lower EC2 spend, and production lead-time reduction make the impact credible. The document also accurately reflects the Original Candidate Information; no unsupported skills, tools, certifications, or experiences were detected. The main content weakness is that one particularly relevant analytical achievement—using k6 to simulate 300,000 concurrent players and resolving a connection-pool limit before launch—is only partially represented. The CV could also make platform architecture, system design, and stakeholder leadership more explicit using evidence already present.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-compatible: it uses conventional headings, a simple text structure, standard job titles, readable date formats, and strong keyword coverage for AWS, Terraform, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, observability, Linux, reliability, and incident management. Its likely AI/ATS screening probability is high for the infrastructure, AWS, Terraform, Kubernetes, reliability, and technical leadership portions of the role. Screening will be weaker for exact terms that are absent from both the CV and the candidate information, especially Terragrunt, mutual TLS/mTLS, SSL/TLS, IoT or automotive integration, and JVM. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than document defects and should not be added without evidence. The existing AWS line is keyword-rich, although networking could be made more visible by explicitly grouping VPC and related services under a networking label.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns very well with hands-on infrastructure engineering, AWS cloud environment design and operation, Terraform, Linux, observability, platform reliability, technical leadership, stakeholder alignment, analytical problem-solving, and clear communication. It also fits Corvale's engineering-led culture through evidence of end-to-end ownership, self-service enablement, technical initiative leadership, and collaboration with product leadership. The strongest relevant examples are the internal developer platform, the SLO/error-budget programme, the Karpenter cost initiative, and the technical lead role. The candidate does not show Terragrunt, mTLS/SSL/TLS, IoT or automotive/remote-device integration, or a JVM-specific background. The CV does show adjacent backend/platform development through Go and Python service templates and a Go controller, but not JVM experience. These are genuine gaps against the advertisement, not rewriting issues.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE CONTENT IMPROVEMENT
1. In the Brightwater Games experience section, expand the existing k6 bullet to include the strongest analytical result from the Original Candidate Information. Replace:
“Ran k6 load tests and led launch capacity planning, including tests simulating 300,000 concurrent players; identified and resolved a connection-pool limit before launch.”
If retaining the current wording, ensure the final version explicitly includes both “300,000 concurrent players” and “identified and resolved a connection-pool limit before launch.” This gives direct evidence of analytical thinking, systems diagnosis, performance testing, and production readiness.

MINOR, TARGETED ALIGNMENT ENHANCEMENTS
2. In the Professional Summary, make the job's “cloud environment design and operation” and “system design” terminology more explicit without adding unsupported experience. For example, change:
“Hands-on expertise in Terraform and AWS cloud environments, with a track record of leading technical initiatives from proposal to production.”
to:
“Hands-on expertise in Terraform and AWS cloud environment design and operation, with experience shaping platform architecture and leading technical initiatives from proposal to production.”
This accurately reflects the existing internal developer platform and EKS work while improving keyword alignment.

3. In the Core Skills section, add a distinct networking label using technologies already present in the CV. For example, change the first line to:
“Cloud infrastructure and networking: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront), cloud environment design and operation.”
Do not add mTLS, SSL/TLS, certificate management, Terragrunt, IoT, or JVM because they are not supported by the Original Candidate Information.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured technical CV with clear progression, measurable outcomes, relevant certifications, and credible platform engineering achievements. The Tallybrook section is particularly effective: it demonstrates technical leadership, scale, self-service infrastructure, reliability improvements, and cost reduction. The document is concise and professional. The main content issue is that the stated “10 years of experience” is not supported by the employment history shown, which begins in 2019 after the Pennine Hosting role was removed. The CV also uses “systems architecture” as a capability without providing a concrete example in the experience section.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly overall: it uses conventional headings, plain text job titles, consistent dates, standard bullet points, and strong keywords including AWS, EKS, Terraform, Kubernetes, GitOps, Crossplane, observability, SLOs, incident management, Go, Python, and Linux. Its AI-screening probability is high for AWS/platform/SRE roles, but moderate rather than high for this specific vacancy because “Terragrunt,” “mTLS,” “SSL/TLS,” security, and explicit networking terminology are absent. Do not add those terms unless supported by the candidate's material. “Cloud infrastructure,” “cloud environment design,” and “systems architecture” should be tied to specific evidence to make them more credible to both ATS and human reviewers.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV strongly matches hands-on infrastructure engineering, AWS cloud operation, Terraform, Kubernetes, platform reliability, technical leadership, observability, and support for product teams. It also provides evidence of stakeholder alignment through the error-budget policy agreed with product leadership and adoption of the internal developer platform by all 14 product teams. The quantified operational scale and cost/reliability results fit Corvale's engineering-led, end-to-end ownership culture. Gaps in the candidate material are strong Terragrunt experience, mTLS/SSL/TLS and certificate management, train/vehicle, IoT or remote-device integration, practical security examples, JVM/backend development, and virtual-machine experience. These are capability gaps rather than document defects. Linux is supported and shown in the CV.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL:
1. In the Professional Summary section, remove the unsupported/inconsistent phrase “with 10 years of experience in infrastructure engineering” because the visible employment history now starts in 2019. Replace it with “Senior platform and reliability engineer with six years of experience running Kubernetes platforms on AWS” or “Senior platform and reliability engineer with extensive experience in infrastructure engineering, including six years running Kubernetes platforms on AWS.” This preserves the supported AWS/Kubernetes experience without creating a chronology question.
2. In the Professional Summary and Core Skills sections, remove or substantiate the phrase “systems architecture.” The Original Candidate Information does not provide a specific systems-architecture example. If no further evidence exists, change “systems architecture” to the supported “infrastructure engineering and cloud infrastructure operation.” Do not present systems architecture as an established skill without an experience bullet supporting it.

MEANINGFUL ENHANCEMENTS:
3. In the Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd section, revise the platform-adoption bullet to make stakeholder alignment more explicit while staying truthful: “Enabled adoption of the developer platform across all 14 product teams, reducing the time to take a new service to production from approximately two weeks to under one day.” This wording is already supported and should be retained; ensure it remains prominent because it directly demonstrates bringing product stakeholders along.
4. In the Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd section, revise “Technical lead for a five-person platform team” to “Technical lead for a five-person platform team, coordinating platform priorities and technical delivery across 14 product teams.” Use this only if “coordinating platform priorities and technical delivery” accurately describes the existing tech-lead responsibilities; do not imply line management.
5. In the Core Skills section, retain “Linux” as a standalone searchable keyword rather than relying only on the “Platform and systems” line. For example, use “Linux systems, Kubernetes, Helm, Kustomize, Argo CD, Karpenter.” This preserves the supported Linux requirement after the Pennine Hosting role was removed.
6. In the Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd section, consider adding the supported implementation detail to the SLO bullet: “using Prometheus recording rules and Sloth” and “burn-rate alerts.” A truthful version would be: “Led the SLO programme for the 20 most critical services, using Prometheus recording rules and Sloth to introduce burn-rate alerts and an error-budget policy agreed with product leadership; reduced on-call pages by approximately 60%.” This improves technical specificity and demonstrates analytical reliability work.
